headline: Rain moves in this afternoon and evening with a likely tenth to half inch of much-needed rain tonight into early Sunday, followed by a very warm Monday and then a much cooler, unsettled stretch midweek.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Clouds thicken Saturday over the Charlotte area and the rest of the region, with highs near normal and northeast winds gusting around 20–30 mph east of the mountains. Rain spreads from south to north this afternoon into this evening, though its exact arrival time is uncertain. Rain becomes likely across most of the area Saturday night into early Sunday, with a beneficial 0.1–0.5 inch, the highest amounts in northeast Georgia and the western South Carolina Upstate.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Rain chances diminish through Sunday as highs climb above normal. Monday is the warmest day of the week, with highs more than 10 degrees above normal as skies clear and winds coming down off the mountains warm the air, though a front could bring brief, light showers to the North Carolina mountains Monday afternoon and evening. That mostly dry cold front crosses Monday night into Tuesday, bringing much cooler air, with temperatures near to below normal from Tuesday on.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Temperatures stay near to below normal through the end of the week. The models disagree on a complex, highly amplified pattern from midweek on, but there is some agreement that a coastal low will develop off the Southeast coast Wednesday into Thursday, raising rain chances across much of the area, with amounts still uncertain. If enough cold air is in place early Wednesday, the North Carolina mountains could see some wintry precipitation at the start, with any accumulation likely minimal.

watch_for: Rain arrival timing this afternoon and evening, with the heaviest amounts toward northeast Georgia and the western Upstate.
Rain chances and possible wintry precipitation in the North Carolina mountains Wednesday into Thursday.
confidence: Forecasters are fairly confident in tonight's rain, a warm Monday and the cooldown Tuesday, but confidence is low from midweek onward because the models disagree.
